domain_label: Formal Knowledge Representation & Reasoning — Knowledge Representation & Ontology Engineering subdomain
purpose: Provide a session-bounded, subdomain-grain ontology of Formal Knowledge Representation & Reasoning work units (problem framing, formalism selection, expressivity-vs-tractability analysis, OWA/CWA stance, TBox/ABox modeling, FOL decidable-fragment encoding, rule/LP/Datalog/SWRL design, frames and semantic networks, nonmonotonic reasoning, reasoning-service specification, reasoner selection, consistency debugging, explanation/provenance, ontology reuse/alignment, query answering, governance/versioning, and evaluation) to plan, evaluate, sequence, validate, and lock the design of decidable knowledge bases for finding, retrieving, and synthesizing authoritative knowledge.
assumptions: Parent domain is knowledge_representation_and_ontology_engineering; this KB models the Formal Knowledge Representation & Reasoning subdomain at subdomain grain.
No observed dataset, benchmark, or expert-judgment input was supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors.
Each node is a single KR&R work unit, method, or decision area sized for one heavy reasoning session.
Reasoning tasks, scale targets, and data completeness are parameters the workflow profiles before locking structure.
Decidable, tractable representation is the default goal; full FOL is used only where a decidable fragment cannot express a required inference.
exclusions: Statistical/neural knowledge representation, embeddings, and learned KGs (covered by other KBs).
Probabilistic graphical models and Bayesian reasoning beyond qualitative uncertainty.
Full-text and vector retrieval, ranking, and indexing internals.
Domain-specific subject content authoring for any one discipline.
Reasoner internal implementation and low-level performance tuning beyond selection.

competency_questions.question: What queries and inferences must the knowledge base support?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: KR_PROBLEM_FRAMING present with competency-question and required-inference outputs

competency_questions.question: Which representation formalism fits the required inferences and scale?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FORMALISM_SELECT and KR_PROBLEM_FRAMING present with a formalism decision record

competency_questions.question: Is the chosen fragment decidable and tractable for the target services and scale?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EXPRESSIVITY_TRACTABILITY present with a complexity/decidability verdict

competency_questions.question: How are concepts, roles, and individuals modeled in the TBox and ABox?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TBOX_MODELING and ABOX_MODELING present with axiom and assertion outputs

competency_questions.question: Which derivations should be axioms versus rules (LP/Datalog/SWRL)?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RULE_SYSTEM_DESIGN and SWRL_RULE_INTEGRATION present with a rule-vs-axiom partition

competency_questions.question: Should the KB use open-world or closed-world assumptions, and where?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OWA_CWA_STANCE present with a documented per-predicate closure policy

competency_questions.question: How are defaults and exceptions handled without corrupting strict entailment?
Which reasoning services answer each competency query?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REASONING_SERVICES present mapping queries to named services

competency_questions.question: Which reasoner and calculus meet the fragment, services, and scale?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REASONER_SELECTION present with a calculus rationale

competency_questions.question: How are inconsistencies and surprising entailments diagnosed and explained?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONSISTENCY_DEBUG and EXPLANATION_PROVENANCE present with justifications

competency_questions.question: How should external ontologies be reused and data queried via the ontology?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ONTOLOGY_REUSE_ALIGN and QUERY_ANSWERING present with import and rewriting plans

competency_questions.question: Where does the model risk undecidability or intractability?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EXPRESSIVITY_TRACTABILITY, FORMALISM_SELECT, SWRL_RULE_INTEGRATION present with decidability notes

competency_questions.question: How are ontology and rule changes governed, versioned, and explained?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GOVERNANCE_VERSIONING and EXPLANATION_PROVENANCE present with impact records

competency_questions.question: Is the knowledge base ready for release against competency and quality criteria?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ONTOLOGY_EVALUATION and GOVERNANCE_VERSIONING present with a release-readiness verdict

glossary.definition: terminological axioms defining concepts, roles, and their relationships
assertional axioms about individuals, their types, and role fillers
decidable fragment of FOL with concepts, roles, and individuals underlying OWL
expressive description logic underlying OWL 2 DL with roles, nominals, qualified cardinality
reasoning service deciding whether one concept is a subconcept of another
whether a concept can have at least one instance in some model
computing the complete inferred subsumption hierarchy of all named concepts
deciding whether an individual is an instance of a concept
unstated facts are unknown rather than false
facts not entailed are taken as false
inference where adding facts can retract previously drawn conclusions
function-free Horn-clause language for recursive, decidable derivations
Semantic Web Rule Language combining OWL with Horn-like rules, decidable when DL-safe
a rule restricted to named individuals so the combined ontology stays decidable
a minimal set of axioms entailing a given consequence (e.g. MUPS for unsatisfiability)
nonmonotonic technique minimizing the extension of abnormality predicates

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from established KR&R literature (Brachman & Levesque 2004; Baader et al. Description Logic Handbook; Staab & Studer Handbook on Ontologies 2009); no measured dataset supplied.
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors, not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Frame the modeling problem: what queries must be answered, what entities and relations exist, and what reasoning the application demands.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when new competency questions or reasoning tasks are introduced

pros.claim: prevents choosing a formalism that cannot express the needed inferences
pros.example: modeling part-of as a plain property when transitive part-of reasoning is required

cons.claim: framing errors propagate into every downstream axiom and reasoner choice
cons.example: omitting a temporal query forces a later re-axiomatization

failure_modes: queries inferred from data shape not user need
acceptance_tests: competency questions enumerated and answerable in principle
required inferences classified by task type
revisit_triggers: reasoning task changes from retrieval to classification

nodes.definition: Select the representation formalism family (DL/OWL profile, FOL fragment, rules/LP/Datalog, frames, semantic network) matching expressivity and tractability needs.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when an inference cannot be expressed or reasoning misses tractability targets

pros.claim: binds expressivity to a decidable, tractable enough fragment up front
pros.example: choosing OWL 2 EL for large biomedical TBoxes to keep classification polynomial

cons.claim: a wrong formalism commitment forces costly re-encoding of all axioms
cons.example: picking OWL 2 DL then needing nonmonotonic defaults it cannot express

acceptance_tests: selected fragment can express all required inferences
tractability class documented for target scale

nodes.definition: Analyze the expressivity-versus-tractability tradeoff and map required constructs to a complexity/decidability class for the target reasoning services.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when constructs change or scale targets shift

pros.claim: flags undecidable or intractable combinations before authoring
pros.example: detecting that role composition plus nominals risks undecidability

cons.claim: complexity bounds are worst-case and may misjudge practical performance
cons.example: EXPTIME-complete SROIQ often classifies real ontologies quickly

acceptance_tests: each required construct mapped to its complexity contribution
decidability verdict justified for the fragment
revisit_triggers: scale grows by an order of magnitude

nodes.definition: Decide and document the open-world vs closed-world assumption and unique-name assumption stance that govern how absence of information is interpreted.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when closure or completeness expectations change

pros.claim: prevents misreading missing data as false under OWL's open world
pros.example: not concluding a patient is allergy-free merely because no allergy is asserted

cons.claim: mixing OWA semantics with CWA validation expectations confuses stakeholders
cons.example: users expecting closed-world counts get incomplete answers from a DL reasoner

failure_modes: assuming CWA inside an OWL TBox
forgetting UNA absence allows individual merges
acceptance_tests: world assumption stated and consistent with chosen formalism
predicates needing closure listed with mechanism

nodes.definition: Model the terminological box: concepts, concept hierarchy, role definitions, and class axioms (subsumption, equivalence, disjointness, restrictions).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when concepts, roles, or class axioms are added or changed

pros.claim: a sound TBox lets the classifier derive an explicit subsumption hierarchy
pros.example: disjointness axioms let the reasoner flag a concept that is unsatisfiable

cons.claim: over-axiomatized TBoxes raise reasoning cost and unsatisfiability risk
cons.example: global cardinality restrictions interacting to make many classes unsatisfiable

failure_modes: missing disjointness so nothing is contradictory
acceptance_tests: TBox classifies without unintended unsatisfiable classes
each modeled relation has documented domain/range or restriction

nodes.definition: Model the assertional box: individuals, type assertions, role assertions, and (in)equality assertions consistent with the TBox.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when instance data or identity policy changes

pros.claim: well-typed assertions enable instance checking and realization
pros.example: classifying an individual into all inferred types via the reasoner

cons.claim: without UNA, distinct individuals can be unexpectedly merged or kept apart
cons.example: two individuals collapsed by a functional role causing wrong entailments

failure_modes: relying on closed-world counts over an open ABox
acceptance_tests: ABox is consistent against the TBox
identity assumptions (sameAs/differentFrom) made explicit where needed

nodes.definition: Encode requirements in first-order logic and select a decidable fragment (two-variable, guarded, DL-as-FOL) when full FOL expressivity is unnecessary.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when axioms or the target fragment change

pros.claim: staying in a decidable fragment guarantees terminating reasoning
pros.example: mapping to the guarded fragment to keep entailment decidable

cons.claim: full FOL is semidecidable so naive axioms may never terminate
cons.example: an unrestricted transitivity-plus-equality axiom set with no decision procedure

failure_modes: leaving fragment unknowingly via function symbols
acceptance_tests: axiom set shown to lie in a named decidable fragment or flagged otherwise
no construct silently escapes the fragment
revisit_triggers: new axiom uses an out-of-fragment construct

nodes.definition: Design production rules, logic-programming clauses, or Datalog programs for derivations not naturally captured by the schema axioms.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when derivation rules or their negation/recursion change

pros.claim: rules express derivations (e.g. property chains, defaults) DLs cannot
pros.example: a Datalog rule deriving ancestor from parent recursively

cons.claim: mixing nonmonotonic rules with monotonic axioms breaks semantic clarity
cons.example: negation-as-failure in rules contradicting open-world TBox entailments

acceptance_tests: rule program is stratified or its semantics declared
rule-vs-axiom partition documented and non-overlapping

nodes.definition: Integrate SWRL or rule extensions with the ontology under DL-safety constraints so rule firing stays decidable over known individuals.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when SWRL rules or their safety scope change

pros.claim: DL-safe rules add expressivity while preserving decidability
pros.example: binding a property-chain rule to named individuals to stay decidable

cons.claim: unsafe SWRL rules make the combined logic undecidable
cons.example: a rule quantifying over anonymous individuals losing decidability

acceptance_tests: all SWRL rules are DL-safe or the relaxation is justified
combined ontology+rules still terminates

nodes.definition: Model frame-based or semantic-network structures (slots, fillers, defaults, inheritance, IS-A/instance links) and map their semantics to a logical formalism.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when frame structure or inheritance policy changes

pros.claim: frames give intuitive structure and default inheritance for prototypes
pros.example: a Bird frame with default flies=true overridden by Penguin

cons.claim: informal inheritance semantics cause ambiguous default overriding
cons.example: unclear whether a more specific frame cancels or merges inherited slots

failure_modes: link types left untyped causing ambiguous inference
acceptance_tests: each link type has a defined logical reading
default/override policy is explicit
revisit_triggers: semantic-net link reused with new meaning

nodes.definition: Design nonmonotonic reasoning (default logic, circumscription, closed-world assumption) for defeasible conclusions that retract under new evidence.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when defaults, exceptions, or closure policy change

pros.claim: captures defeasible defaults that retract when exceptions arrive
pros.example: concluding birds fly by default, retracted for an asserted penguin

cons.claim: multiple default extensions create nondeterministic or conflicting conclusions
cons.example: two normal defaults yielding incompatible extensions with no preference rule

failure_modes: unbounded extensions with no preference order
mixing nonmonotonic defaults into monotonic entailment silently
acceptance_tests: default conflicts resolved by explicit specificity/priority
nonmonotonic scope isolated from monotonic axioms

nodes.definition: Specify and configure standard reasoning services: subsumption, satisfiability, consistency, classification, instance checking, and realization.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when required reasoning services or queries change

pros.claim: standard services turn axioms into answerable inference queries
pros.example: classification builds the inferred hierarchy used by downstream apps

cons.claim: some services are reducible to others, hiding true cost
cons.example: instance checking reduced to consistency masking per-individual expense

failure_modes: requesting services the fragment cannot answer efficiently
acceptance_tests: each required query maps to a named reasoning service
service outputs validated against expected entailments

nodes.definition: Select a reasoner and reasoning calculus (tableau, consequence-based, resolution, materialization) matching the fragment, services, and scale.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when fragment, services, or scale targets change

pros.claim: a profile-matched reasoner meets latency targets at scale
pros.example: using a consequence-based EL reasoner for million-class classification

cons.claim: reasoner-specific behavior reduces portability across engines
cons.example: relying on a reasoner's nonstandard pellet-specific feature

acceptance_tests: reasoner supports the chosen fragment and services
performance meets the documented scale target on a representative load

nodes.definition: Detect and repair inconsistency and unsatisfiable concepts using justifications, modularization, and minimal-conflict (MUPS/MIPS) analysis.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when axioms change or new inconsistencies appear

pros.claim: justifications localize the few axioms causing an unsatisfiable class
pros.example: a MUPS of 3 axioms explaining why class C is unsatisfiable

cons.claim: many overlapping justifications make repair choice ambiguous
cons.example: dozens of MUPS for one class, each suggesting a different deletion

failure_modes: repairing by deleting the wrong axiom
ignoring that one fix can create new unsatisfiabilities
acceptance_tests: each unsatisfiable class has at least one extracted justification
post-repair reasoner run shows no unintended unsatisfiable classes

nodes.definition: Produce human-checkable explanations and provenance for entailments so derived conclusions can be audited and trusted.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when entailments are disputed or provenance sources change

pros.claim: explanations let reviewers validate surprising entailments
pros.example: showing the 4-axiom chain that entailed an unexpected subsumption

cons.claim: minimal justifications can omit the intuitive cause
cons.example: a justification that is logically minimal but not the modeling error

acceptance_tests: each surprising entailment has a retrievable justification
provenance links each axiom to its source

nodes.definition: Reuse and align external ontologies/vocabularies (imports, upper ontologies, mappings) while controlling imported axiom risk.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when imported ontologies or mappings change

pros.claim: reusing curated ontologies saves modeling effort and aids interoperability
pros.example: importing an upper ontology to align top-level categories

cons.claim: importing brings in axioms that can cause unexpected entailments or inconsistency
cons.example: an imported disjointness axiom making local classes unsatisfiable

failure_modes: importing entire heavy ontologies for a few terms
acceptance_tests: each import justified and scoped to needed modules
imported axioms screened for inconsistency before commit

nodes.definition: Design conjunctive query answering, including ontology-based data access with DL-Lite/QL and query rewriting over data sources.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when queries or data sources change

pros.claim: DL-Lite enables first-order query rewriting over live databases
pros.example: rewriting a query so a SQL engine answers it with ontology entailments

cons.claim: certain-answer semantics under OWA differ from SQL closed-world results
cons.example: users surprised that a count returns only certain answers

failure_modes: choosing a fragment whose query answering is intractable
acceptance_tests: each competency query is expressible and answerable in the fragment
rewriting preserves certain-answer semantics

nodes.definition: Establish governance: versioning, change impact analysis, deprecation policy, and locking for the ontology and rule base.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the ontology or rule base is versioned or deprecated

pros.claim: stable IRIs and impact analysis prevent breaking downstream consumers
pros.example: deprecating a class without deleting its IRI to keep references valid

cons.claim: governance overhead slows iteration if too heavy
cons.example: every minor label change forced through full impact analysis

failure_modes: no impact analysis before a breaking change
acceptance_tests: version increments follow a documented policy
each breaking change has an impact-analysis record

nodes.definition: Evaluate the knowledge base against competency questions, consistency, coverage, and inference-quality criteria before release.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when competency questions or axioms change materially

pros.claim: competency-question testing confirms the KB answers its intended queries
pros.example: verifying each CQ returns the expected certain answers

cons.claim: passing CQs does not prove absence of unintended entailments
cons.example: CQs all pass while a hidden disjointness gap allows wrong inferences

acceptance_tests: all competency questions answered as specified
no unintended entailments in the regression entailment suite

edges.why_related: formalism choice requires the queries and required inferences fixed by framing
edges.risk_of_conflict: framing drift forces re-selecting the formalism
edges.example: competency questions determine whether DL or rules are needed
edges.resolution_rule: source dominates: do not finalize FORMALISM_SELECT before framing is reviewed

edges.why_related: tractability analysis evaluates the constructs of the selected fragment
edges.risk_of_conflict: wrong fragment makes the complexity analysis moot
edges.example: analyzing SROIQ complexity only after OWL-DL is chosen
edges.resolution_rule: source dominates: re-run analysis if formalism changes

edges.why_related: world-assumption stance depends on the semantics of the chosen formalism
edges.benefit_of_coupling: aligns closure policy with formalism semantics
edges.risk_of_conflict: OWL imposes OWA, restricting CWA options
edges.example: choosing CWA needs rules/LP not pure OWL
edges.resolution_rule: source dominates: stance must match formalism semantics

edges.why_related: TBox axioms must stay within the analyzed tractable fragment
edges.risk_of_conflict: authoring beyond the fragment breaks reasoning
edges.example: avoiding role composition that escapes EL
edges.resolution_rule: source dominates: TBox constructs constrained by the analysis

edges.why_related: FOL fragment encoding follows from the chosen formalism family
edges.benefit_of_coupling: keeps encoding in a decidable fragment
edges.risk_of_conflict: encoding outside the fragment loses decidability
edges.example: mapping to the guarded fragment per the decision record
edges.resolution_rule: source dominates: encoding must respect the selected fragment

edges.why_related: ABox assertions must conform to the TBox vocabulary and axioms
edges.risk_of_conflict: asserting against an unstable TBox forces rework
edges.example: an individual typed by a TBox class
edges.resolution_rule: source dominates: TBox stabilized before ABox is finalized

edges.why_related: world and UNA stance bound how ABox identity and completeness are read
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring stance causes wrong identity merges
edges.example: UNA absence allowing sameAs inference
edges.resolution_rule: stance dominates: ABox identity follows the documented stance

edges.why_related: rules reference TBox vocabulary and complement its axioms
edges.benefit_of_coupling: rules add derivations the TBox cannot express
edges.risk_of_conflict: rules over an unstable vocabulary need rewriting
edges.example: a rule deriving a property chain over TBox roles
edges.resolution_rule: source dominates: vocabulary fixed before rule authoring

edges.why_related: negation-as-failure in rules depends on the closure stance
edges.benefit_of_coupling: aligns rule negation with closure policy
edges.risk_of_conflict: CWA negation conflicting with OWA TBox
edges.example: NAF deriving non-membership only under closure
edges.resolution_rule: stance dominates: rule negation must honor closure policy

edges.why_related: SWRL integration packages designed rules under DL-safety
edges.benefit_of_coupling: binds rules to the ontology decidably
edges.risk_of_conflict: unsafe integration loses decidability
edges.example: DL-safe SWRL over named individuals
edges.resolution_rule: source dominates: rules designed before safe integration

edges.why_related: the TBox bounds which individuals SWRL rules may safely range over
edges.risk_of_conflict: rules over inferred individuals break safety
edges.example: restricting rule variables to known individuals
edges.resolution_rule: TBox dominates: safety scope set by TBox/ABox individuals

edges.why_related: nonmonotonic design extends the closure stance with defaults
edges.risk_of_conflict: defaults conflicting with closure stance
edges.example: CWA as a special case of circumscription
edges.resolution_rule: source dominates: defaults built on the closure decision

edges.why_related: frame/semantic-net structures realize the entities and relations from framing
edges.risk_of_conflict: modeling before framing yields ad-hoc frames
edges.example: frames for prototype entities identified in framing
edges.resolution_rule: source dominates: framing precedes frame design

edges.why_related: reasoning services operate over the TBox to classify and check satisfiability
edges.risk_of_conflict: services over an unstable TBox waste runs
edges.example: classification of the TBox hierarchy
edges.resolution_rule: source dominates: TBox stable before service runs are trusted

edges.why_related: instance checking and realization require the ABox assertions
edges.risk_of_conflict: services over incomplete ABox mislead
edges.example: realizing an individual's inferred types
edges.resolution_rule: source dominates: ABox finalized before instance services

edges.why_related: reasoner and calculus must match the analyzed complexity class
edges.benefit_of_coupling: ensures the engine can meet performance
edges.risk_of_conflict: a reasoner mismatched to the fragment fails
edges.example: an EL reasoner for an EL profile
edges.resolution_rule: source dominates: reasoner choice constrained by complexity profile

edges.why_related: the required services determine which reasoner capabilities are needed
edges.risk_of_conflict: selecting a reasoner lacking a needed service
edges.example: needing explanation forces an explanation-capable reasoner
edges.resolution_rule: source dominates: services specified before reasoner is locked

edges.why_related: debugging consumes consistency and classification results to localize faults
edges.risk_of_conflict: debugging without service output is blind
edges.example: using classification to find unsatisfiable classes
edges.resolution_rule: source dominates: run services before debugging

edges.why_related: explanations are derived from the entailments the services produce
edges.risk_of_conflict: explaining without entailment output is impossible
edges.example: justifying an inferred subsumption
edges.resolution_rule: source dominates: entailments produced before explanation

edges.why_related: reuse and alignment extend or map the local TBox
edges.benefit_of_coupling: reuse saves modeling and aids interoperability
edges.risk_of_conflict: aligning to an unstable TBox forces remapping
edges.example: mapping local classes to an upper ontology
edges.resolution_rule: source dominates: stabilize core TBox before external alignment

edges.why_related: query answering rewrites queries using TBox axioms
edges.risk_of_conflict: queries over an unstable TBox need rewriting
edges.example: DL-Lite rewriting using TBox inclusions
edges.resolution_rule: source dominates: TBox fixed before query rewriting

edges.why_related: governance versions and locks the authored TBox and rules
edges.risk_of_conflict: versioning before content exists is premature
edges.example: incrementing version on a breaking axiom change
edges.resolution_rule: source dominates: substantive content precedes governance lock

edges.why_related: evaluation requires a consistent, debugged knowledge base
edges.benefit_of_coupling: ensures evaluation runs on a sound KB
edges.risk_of_conflict: evaluating an inconsistent KB is meaningless
edges.example: no unsatisfiable classes before CQ testing
edges.resolution_rule: source dominates: debug before evaluation

edges.why_related: evaluation tests competency questions via reasoning-service outputs
edges.benefit_of_coupling: confirms the KB answers intended queries
edges.risk_of_conflict: evaluating without service output proves nothing
edges.example: checking CQ certain answers
edges.resolution_rule: source dominates: services run before evaluation

edges.why_related: imported and aligned axioms change the probability of inconsistency
edges.risk_of_conflict: imports can inject contradictions
edges.example: an imported disjointness making a class unsatisfiable
edges.resolution_rule: run debugging after each import; reject imports that cannot be repaired

edges.why_related: nonmonotonic conclusions are not standard monotonic entailments and bound which services apply
edges.benefit_of_coupling: keeps monotonic and defeasible inference separate
edges.risk_of_conflict: mixing breaks soundness of standard services
edges.example: a default conclusion that a classifier would not entail
edges.resolution_rule: monotonic services dominate; defeasible layer runs separately with its own semantics

edges.why_related: the chosen FOL fragment constrains which calculus/prover is decidable
edges.benefit_of_coupling: matches prover to a decidable fragment
edges.risk_of_conflict: a prover outside the fragment may not terminate
edges.example: a resolution prover for a guarded-fragment encoding
edges.resolution_rule: fragment dominates: prover must decide the fragment

edges.why_related: frames/semantic nets and TBox concepts model overlapping structure
edges.benefit_of_coupling: aids deduplication and migration to logic
edges.risk_of_conflict: duplicating concepts across both representations
edges.example: a frame slot equivalent to a DL role
edges.resolution_rule: prefer the formal TBox where reasoning is required; keep frames for UI/prototyping

edges.why_related: richer TBox expressivity trades off against tractable reasoning
edges.risk_of_conflict: unbounded expressivity makes reasoning intractable
edges.example: adding nominals/inverses pushing EL into a costlier fragment
edges.resolution_rule: tractability dominates unless an inference is mandatory and unsubstitutable; record the decision

edges.why_related: open-world entailment conflicts with closed-world negation-as-failure in rules
edges.risk_of_conflict: silent mixing yields contradictory conclusions
edges.example: NAF deriving non-allergy while OWL leaves it open
edges.resolution_rule: isolate NAF to DL-safe/closed predicates; OWA governs the open TBox layer

edges.why_related: defeasible defaults conflict with monotonic TBox entailment
edges.risk_of_conflict: defaults asserted as strict axioms corrupt entailment
edges.example: modeling 'birds fly' as a strict subsumption
edges.resolution_rule: strict axioms dominate; defaults live in the nonmonotonic layer with explicit exceptions

edges.why_related: imported foreign axioms conflict with local modeling commitments
edges.risk_of_conflict: imports override or contradict local axioms
edges.example: an upper-ontology axiom contradicting a local restriction
edges.resolution_rule: local commitments dominate; align via mappings, not by absorbing conflicting imports

edges.why_related: a desired reasoner's limits conflict with the needed expressivity
edges.benefit_of_coupling: forces realistic expressivity within engine limits
edges.risk_of_conflict: picking a reasoner first constrains modeling
edges.example: a fast EL reasoner that cannot handle needed inverses
edges.resolution_rule: expressivity requirements dominate; choose a reasoner that meets them or downgrade deliberately

edges.why_related: stability/locking pressure conflicts with iterative remodeling needs
edges.risk_of_conflict: over-locking blocks needed corrections
edges.example: a frozen TBox blocking a necessary disjointness fix
edges.resolution_rule: correctness fixes dominate via impact analysis and version increment

edges.why_related: debugging findings trigger revisiting TBox axioms to repair faults
edges.benefit_of_coupling: closes the loop on unsatisfiable classes
edges.risk_of_conflict: unbounded re-edits without revalidation loop
edges.example: removing an axiom in a justification set
edges.resolution_rule: stop when no unsatisfiable classes remain and CQs still pass; max repair cycles bounded

edges.why_related: evaluation gaps trigger revisiting the problem framing and competency questions
edges.benefit_of_coupling: aligns the KB with real needs
edges.risk_of_conflict: endless reframing without acceptance criteria
edges.example: a failed CQ revealing a missing requirement
edges.resolution_rule: stop when all competency questions pass; reframing requires a recorded gap

edges.why_related: evaluation findings trigger TBox corrections before release
edges.risk_of_conflict: re-modeling loops without a stop gate
edges.example: an unintended entailment prompting an axiom fix
edges.resolution_rule: stop when the entailment regression suite passes; bounded iterations

edges.why_related: service performance results trigger reconsidering the reasoner choice
edges.risk_of_conflict: reasoner churn without measured need
edges.example: missed latency target prompting an engine switch
edges.resolution_rule: stop when latency targets are met on representative load; one switch per regression

edges.why_related: query-answering gaps trigger TBox adjustments to make queries answerable
edges.risk_of_conflict: TBox churn driven by ad-hoc queries
edges.example: adding a property to support a needed query
edges.resolution_rule: stop when all competency queries are answerable; changes go through impact analysis

edges.why_related: explanations of surprising entailments trigger targeted debugging
edges.benefit_of_coupling: focuses repair on the real cause
edges.risk_of_conflict: chasing every explanation indefinitely
edges.example: a justification revealing a modeling error
edges.resolution_rule: stop when the surprising entailment is corrected or accepted with a record

conflict_axes.trigger: a required inference needs a construct that raises the complexity class
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: prefer the least expressive fragment that still answers the mandatory inferences; add expressivity only with a recorded justification
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: adding the construct makes reasoning intractable at target scale
conflict_axes.example: adding role composition that pushes EL into a costlier fragment

conflict_axes.trigger: validation/negation needs closure while entailment needs open-world semantics
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: OWA governs the entailment layer; closure is applied only to explicitly declared complete predicates
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: closure changes the truth value of a safety-critical conclusion
conflict_axes.example: counting allergies under CWA versus leaving them open under OWA

conflict_axes.trigger: defaults must be captured but standard reasoning must stay sound
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: strict axioms dominate the monotonic layer; defaults live in a separate defeasible layer with explicit exceptions
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a default would otherwise be asserted as a strict subsumption
conflict_axes.example: 'birds fly' modeled as default with penguin exception, not as a strict axiom

conflict_axes.trigger: a derivation can be modeled either as a class axiom or as a rule
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: prefer schema axioms when the reasoner can express them; use DL-safe rules only for derivations DL cannot capture
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: the rule choice changes decidability of the combined logic
conflict_axes.example: property chains as role axioms versus a SWRL rule

conflict_axes.trigger: importing external axioms versus retaining full local control
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: local correctness dominates; reuse via scoped imports and mappings, never by absorbing conflicting axioms
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: an import injects inconsistency or unintended entailments
conflict_axes.example: importing an upper ontology whose disjointness breaks a local class

conflict_axes.trigger: complete reasoning is too slow at target scale
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: completeness of mandatory inferences dominates; approximate only non-critical inferences with a recorded limitation
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: approximation would drop a safety-relevant entailment
conflict_axes.example: materializing only a tractable profile and flagging dropped inferences

conflict_axes.trigger: a locked artifact needs a correctness fix
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: correctness fixes dominate stability; apply via impact analysis, version increment, and change record
conflict_axes.example: adding a missing disjointness to a frozen TBox version

conflict_axes.trigger: certain answers under OWA omit results users expect from closed-world data
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: certain-answer soundness dominates; communicate incompleteness rather than silently closing the world
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: users make decisions assuming closed-world completeness
conflict_axes.example: a count returning only certain instances under OWA

conflict_axes.trigger: frame/semantic-net intuitions lack precise logical semantics
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: formal semantics dominate where reasoning is required; keep frames for UI/prototyping with a defined logical reading
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: an inference depends on ambiguous default-inheritance semantics
conflict_axes.example: ambiguous slot override semantics affecting an entailment

edge_cases.trigger: an edge or dependency references a node ID that does not exist
edge_cases.example: a dependency pointing to a removed node ID
edge_cases.detection_method: validator cross-checks every reference against node/edge/source ID sets
resolution: restore or rename the referenced ID

edge_cases.trigger: authored axioms silently leave the decidable fragment
edge_cases.example: adding function symbols or unsafe role axioms breaking decidability
edge_cases.detection_method: fragment-membership check on every new construct against the declared fragment
resolution: revert the out-of-fragment construct or move to a richer-but-decidable fragment
record the decision and re-run tractability analysis

edge_cases.trigger: an imported ontology injects contradictory axioms
edge_cases.example: an imported disjointness contradicting a local subsumption
edge_cases.detection_method: run consistency and classification immediately after each import
resolution: scope the import to needed modules
add bridging mappings instead of absorbing conflicting axioms

edge_cases.trigger: closed-world expectations applied to an open-world KB
edge_cases.failure_mode: wrong negative conclusions or missing answers
edge_cases.example: NAF inferring non-membership the open TBox leaves undecided
edge_cases.detection_method: audit each negation and count for the world assumption it relies on

edge_cases.trigger: a defeasible default modeled as a strict axiom
edge_cases.failure_mode: unsound monotonic entailments and unsatisfiability on exceptions
edge_cases.example: 'birds fly' as a strict subsumption making penguins unsatisfiable
edge_cases.detection_method: flag axioms over prototypical classes that lack exception handling
resolution: move the default to the nonmonotonic layer

edge_cases.trigger: a high-risk node lacks acceptance tests
edge_cases.example: the formalism decision shipped without a test that all inferences are expressible
edge_cases.detection_method: validator checks acceptance_tests non-empty for risk_if_wrong>=0.80

edge_cases.trigger: an artifact is hard-locked before validation and review gates pass
edge_cases.failure_mode: locked-in defects requiring change-control to fix
edge_cases.example: freezing the TBox before classification reveals unsatisfiable classes
edge_cases.detection_method: check lock_state transitions against gate-pass conditions

edge_cases.trigger: repair/evaluation loops repeat without a stop condition
edge_cases.example: each repair creating a new unsatisfiable class indefinitely
edge_cases.detection_method: track iteration count against max_iterations and materiality threshold
resolution: escalate to human review when the cap is hit

edge_cases.trigger: dependency edges form a directed cycle
edge_cases.example: TBox depends on rules that depend back on the TBox as dependencies
edge_cases.detection_method: DFS cycle detection over dependency edges and node dependencies
resolution: convert the weaker dependency to sequence or feedback

edge_cases.trigger: an imported ontology or mapping version becomes stale
edge_cases.failure_mode: entailments based on outdated external axioms
edge_cases.example: an upper ontology revised after the mapping was authored
edge_cases.detection_method: compare import version IRIs against current upstream versions

edge_cases.trigger: template placeholder text survives into the KB
edge_cases.example: a node definition left as a schema example string
edge_cases.detection_method: scan raw output for the known placeholder token set

edge_cases.trigger: a computed score disagrees with its formula or a label is illegal
edge_cases.failure_mode: formula inconsistency or illegal evidence label
edge_cases.example: final_importance off by more than tolerance from the weighted sum
edge_cases.detection_method: recompute all derived fields and compare within tolerance; verify labels against the legal set
resolution: recompute derived fields from base metrics

workflow.objective: Fix competency questions, entities, relations, and required inferences
entry_criteria: domain description and use cases available
acceptance_tests: competency questions enumerated
required inferences classified
workflow.do_first_because: framing fixes the requirements that all later choices depend on

workflow.objective: Select formalism, world-assumption, and monotonicity stance
acceptance_tests: selected fragment can express all required inferences
world assumption documented
workflow.do_first_because: formalism and semantics stance bound every downstream modeling choice

workflow.objective: Confirm decidability and tractability of the chosen fragment
acceptance_tests: each construct mapped to complexity
decidability verdict justified
workflow.do_first_because: catching undecidable/intractable combinations before authoring avoids re-encoding

workflow.objective: Author the TBox concept and role axioms within the tractable fragment
acceptance_tests: TBox classifies with no unintended unsatisfiable classes
relations have domain/range or restrictions
workflow.do_first_because: the TBox is the spine that ABox, rules, services, and queries build on

workflow.objective: Add instances, rules, defaults, and frame structures
acceptance_tests: ABox consistent with TBox
rules stratified or DL-safe
workflow.do_first_because: instances, rules, and defaults must conform to a stabilized TBox to avoid rework

workflow.objective: Specify reasoning services and select a matching reasoner
acceptance_tests: each query mapped to a service
reasoner meets scale target on representative load
workflow.do_first_because: services and reasoner must match the fragment before debugging and evaluation

workflow.objective: Reuse/align external ontologies and design query answering
acceptance_tests: imports screened for inconsistency
competency queries expressible
workflow.do_first_because: alignment and queries depend on a stable TBox and consistent imports

acceptance_tests: each unsatisfiable class has a justification
surprising entailments explained
workflow.do_first_because: a sound, explained KB is required before evaluation and release

workflow.objective: Evaluate against competency questions and quality criteria
acceptance_tests: all competency questions answered as specified
no unintended entailments in regression suite
workflow.do_first_because: evaluation must pass before any release lock is taken

workflow.objective: Version, lock, and govern change for release
acceptance_tests: breaking changes have impact analysis
human review completed for high-risk artifacts
workflow.do_first_because: hard lock only after evaluation, human review, and version gates pass

dominance_rules.rule: risk control dominates speed for high-risk nodes
dominance_rules.required_action: run acceptance tests and human review before proceeding
dominance_rules.example: skipping decidability analysis to ship faster

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value node has unmet prerequisites
dominance_rules.rule: dependency order dominates raw value ordering
dominance_rules.required_action: schedule prerequisites first even if lower value
dominance_rules.example: authoring ABox before the TBox is stable

dominance_rules.trigger: a numeric value implies more certainty than evidence supports
dominance_rules.required_action: keep heuristic labels and widen uncertainty intervals
dominance_rules.example: reporting a 0.97 confidence with only heuristic priors

dominance_rules.trigger: an artifact is proposed for lock before QA passes
dominance_rules.required_action: complete evaluation gates before any lock
dominance_rules.example: hard-locking the TBox before classification is clean

dominance_rules.trigger: risk or irreversibility crosses review thresholds
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates automation at thresholds
dominance_rules.required_action: escalate to human review before the irreversible action
dominance_rules.example: auto-deleting an IRI instead of deprecating it

dominance_rules.required_action: stop adding objects until structure is valid
dominance_rules.example: padding near-duplicate nodes that break the count target

dominance_rules.trigger: a claim lacks an eligible source
dominance_rules.required_action: attach SRC_HEURISTIC_PRIOR or remove the claim
dominance_rules.example: labeling a value observed with no dataset

dominance_rules.trigger: a construct raises the complexity class beyond targets
dominance_rules.rule: tractability dominates unless the inference is mandatory and unsubstitutable
dominance_rules.required_action: downgrade the construct or record a justified exception
dominance_rules.example: adding nominals that make classification intractable

dominance_rules.trigger: a default would be asserted as a strict axiom
dominance_rules.rule: strict monotonic soundness dominates default convenience
dominance_rules.required_action: move the default to the nonmonotonic layer with exceptions

dominance_rules.trigger: a convenient sequencing introduces a dependency cycle
dominance_rules.required_action: convert the weaker dependency to sequence/feedback
dominance_rules.example: making TBox depend on rules that depend on the TBox

dominance_rules.trigger: an import conflicts with a local modeling commitment
dominance_rules.required_action: align via mappings, never absorb conflicting axioms
dominance_rules.example: an imported disjointness breaking a local class

anti_rework_rules.rule: Resolve framing before selecting a formalism
anti_rework_rules.rationale: formalism chosen for wrong requirements forces re-encoding
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: formalism record predates approved competency questions
anti_rework_rules.example: picking OWL before queries are known

anti_rework_rules.rationale: analyzing constructs of an unchosen fragment is wasted
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: tractability profile references no decided fragment
anti_rework_rules.example: complexity analysis with no formalism record

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm tractable fragment before TBox authoring
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: TBox uses constructs outside the analyzed fragment
anti_rework_rules.example: adding role composition not covered by the profile

anti_rework_rules.rule: Stabilize the TBox before finalizing the ABox
anti_rework_rules.rationale: assertions over an unstable vocabulary must be redone
anti_rework_rules.example: typing individuals before disjointness is settled

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix TBox vocabulary before authoring rules
anti_rework_rules.rationale: rules over a shifting vocabulary need rewriting
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: rules reference renamed or removed terms
anti_rework_rules.example: a SWRL rule on a deleted role

anti_rework_rules.rule: Decide world assumption before authoring negation/defaults
anti_rework_rules.rationale: negation semantics depend on the closure stance
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: NAF used before a closure policy exists
anti_rework_rules.example: closed-world counts with no stance record

anti_rework_rules.rule: Specify services before locking a reasoner
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a reasoner lacking a needed service forces re-selection
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: reasoner chosen without a service plan
anti_rework_rules.example: picking an engine that cannot explain entailments

anti_rework_rules.rationale: evaluating an inconsistent KB is meaningless
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: evaluation run with unsatisfiable classes present
anti_rework_rules.example: CQ testing over an inconsistent ontology

anti_rework_rules.rule: Screen imports for consistency before committing them
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: import committed without a consistency run
anti_rework_rules.example: absorbing an ontology then finding contradictions

anti_rework_rules.rule: Pass evaluation before any hard lock
anti_rework_rules.rationale: locking defects requires costly change-control to fix
anti_rework_rules.example: freezing the KB before CQs pass

anti_rework_rules.rationale: untraceable artifacts cannot be audited or safely changed
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: traceability matrix incomplete at lock time

iteration_protocol.trigger: validator or reasoner reports a failure
acceptance_tests: every failure mapped to a defect class

action: sort defects by risk and severity
acceptance_tests: queue ordered by risk-adjusted severity
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: queue empty or only sub-threshold low-risk defects

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect touches a high-coupling node
action: run impact analysis on affected nodes/edges
acceptance_tests: impact set lists all downstream nodes
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: impact set stable across a pass

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect is ready for repair
iteration_protocol.detection: map defect class to repair owner
action: route defect to its repair subsystem
acceptance_tests: each defect has a repair owner
no new failures introduced
posterior change exceeds revisit delta only when justified
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: posterior deltas below the revisit threshold

iteration_protocol.trigger: a dependency cycle or invalid edge is found
iteration_protocol.detection: run cycle detection and reference checks
action: convert or remove the offending edge
acceptance_tests: dependency graph is acyclic and references resolve
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no cycles and all references valid

iteration_protocol.trigger: a locked artifact needs a correctness fix
iteration_protocol.detection: detect change request on a locked artifact
acceptance_tests: fix validated before re-lock

iteration_protocol.trigger: risk or iteration cap is reached
action: escalate to human review with a decision record
acceptance_tests: human approval or rejection recorded

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new KB version is produced
iteration_protocol.detection: compare entailments and metrics to the prior version
action: run the entailment regression suite against the baseline
acceptance_tests: no unintended entailment changes
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: regression suite passes against the baseline
